userStories.title: Add Checkpoint Store
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add a durable feature-level checkpoint store that records every green phase and can be reloaded safely after crashes or aborts.

**Motivation** — a story that crashed at step 11 (`adversarial-review`) re-runs `test-writer` + `implementer` + `verifier` + all reviews from scratch, discarding hours of green agent work.

**Approach** — New module `src/execution/checkpoint/`: `types.ts` (`CheckpointRecord`, `StoryCheckpoint`, `TreeState`), `writer.ts` (`CheckpointWriter.recordGreen` durable append via injected `_deps.append`), `reader.ts` (`loadCheckpoints(featureDir)` — longest-valid-prefix parse + latest-`runId` filter → `Map<storyId, StoryCheckpoint>`), barrel `index.ts`.

Reader contract: parse line-by-line, keep the **longest valid prefix** (a torn final line from a crash mid-append is dropped, not fatal); keep only records whose `runId` equals the newest `runId` present; group by `storyId` into `StoryCheckpoint`. A missing or fully-unparseable file yields an empty map — never throws.

`checkpoint.jsonl` — append-only, one JSON object per line, at `~/.nax/<projectKey>/features/<feature>/checkpoint.jsonl`.

**Scope** — In: durable per-green-phase checkpoint at the feature level; durable append writer; longest-valid-prefix + latest-`runId` reader. Out: mid-*phase* resume within a single phase; deriving checkpoints from the events JSONL; a persisted `execution.resume` config field; parallel-mode cross-story coupling.

**Interface**
```typescript
export interface TreeState { headSha: string; dirtyDigest: string; }
export interface StoryCheckpoint {
  storyId: string;
  greenPhases: PhaseKind[];      // phases recorded green, in canonical order
  tree: TreeState;               // tree state captured at last green record
}
```

writer.ts (`CheckpointWriter.recordGreen` durable append via injected `_deps.append`), `reader.ts` (`loadCheckpoints(featureDir)` — longest-valid-prefix parse + latest-`runId` filter → `Map<storyId, StoryCheckpoint>`).
acceptanceCriteria: CheckpointWriter is importable from `src/execution/checkpoint` and is constructable with an injected `_deps` object exposing an `append` function.

Given a `CheckpointWriter`, when `recordGreen(storyId, phase, treeState)` is called, then it invokes `_deps.append` exactly once with a single newline-terminated line whose parsed JSON has `storyId`, `phase`, `headSha`, `dirtyDigest`, `runId`, and `ts` fields equal to the inputs.
Given an injected `_deps.append` that resolves asynchronously, when `recordGreen` is awaited, then it does not resolve until that append has completed.
Given a directory with no `checkpoint.jsonl`, when `loadCheckpoints(featureDir)` runs, then it returns an empty `Map` and does not throw.
Given a `checkpoint.jsonl` whose final line is a truncated JSON fragment, when `loadCheckpoints(featureDir)` runs, then it returns every record from the valid prefix and omits the torn line.
Given records from two different `runId` values, when `loadCheckpoints(featureDir)` runs, then it returns only the records whose `runId` equals the newest `runId` present in the file.

Given valid records for multiple stories, when `loadCheckpoints(featureDir)` runs, then it groups them by `storyId` and returns a `StoryCheckpoint` per story whose `greenPhases` lists that story's recorded phases in canonical order.
Given a well-formed JSON line missing a required field such as `phase`, when `loadCheckpoints(featureDir)` runs, then it skips that line without aborting the parse of other lines.
Given a checkpoint-store operation that raises a checkpoint-specific error, when that error is surfaced to callers, then it is a `NaxError` whose `stage` is `checkpoint`.

routing.reasoning: This story adds a new checkpoint module with append and parse behavior, but it stays mostly isolated to a few additive files and standard dependency-injection seams.

userStories.title: Build Pure Resume Planner
acceptanceCriteria: `buildResumePlan` is importable from `src/execution/checkpoint` and callable with a `StoryCheckpoint` and a `TreeState`.

Given a `StoryCheckpoint` whose `greenPhases` include `implementer` and `verify-scoped` and a matching `TreeState`, when `buildResumePlan` runs, then `skipPhases` contains `implementer` and does not contain `verify-scoped`.
Given the same matching checkpoint and tree, when `buildResumePlan` runs, then `revalidateGates` equals `["verify-scoped", "lint-check", "typecheck-check"]` and `reason` equals `"resume"`.
Given a checkpoint whose `tree.headSha` differs from the current `TreeState.headSha`, when `buildResumePlan` runs, then it returns an empty `skipPhases` array and `reason` equals `"tree-moved"`.

Given a checkpoint whose `tree.dirtyDigest` differs from the current `TreeState.dirtyDigest`, when `buildResumePlan` runs, then it returns an empty `skipPhases` array and `reason` equals `"tree-moved"`.
Given `null` checkpoint input, when `buildResumePlan(null, tree)` runs, then it returns an empty `skipPhases` array and `reason` equals `"no-checkpoint"`.
Given a matching tree and `greenPhases` containing `verify-scoped`, `lint-check`, and `typecheck-check`, when `buildResumePlan` runs, then none of those three cheap gates appears in `skipPhases`.

routing.reasoning: This is a single pure planner file with explicit inputs and outputs, so the lightest route is enough and standard single-session TDD is realistic.

userStories.title: Integrate Resume Into Story Orchestrator
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend the story orchestrator so green phases are checkpointed, resume plans seed `phaseOutputs`, and canonical-loop dispatch skips only the phases that are safe to elide.

**Motivation** — rerunning `nax run` re-scans `prd.json` and restarts every non-`passed` story from the first canonical-order phase (`test-writer` → `implementer` → … → `adversarial-review`).

**Approach** — **Record on pass.** After `runPhase` populates `phaseOutputs[name]` and the phase passes (`phasePassed(...) === true`), the orchestrator calls `CheckpointWriter.recordGreen(storyId, phaseName, treeState)` — one durably-appended JSONL line, flushed to disk before `recordGreen` resolves (and therefore before the next phase begins). Records are written **only after a phase passes**; a mid-phase crash leaves no record for that phase, so it re-runs. This is the correctness invariant. (A SIGKILL mid-append tears only the final line, which the reader's longest-valid-prefix parse drops — so the interrupted phase simply re-runs.)

- **Rehydrate on resume.** `buildResumePlan` returns the set of green **agent** phases to skip. Before the main loop, the orchestrator seeds `phaseOutputs[phase] = { success: true }` for each skip. `phasePassed` treats `{ success: true }` as passed (`phase-eval.ts:43`), and `extractPhaseFindings` returns `[]` for a `success: true` output (`phase-eval.ts:94-96`) — so a seeded phase carries no phantom findings and no phantom gate-failure keys.
- **Skip guard on the main loop.** The main loop (`execution-plan.ts:64-89`) currently runs every phase unconditionally; the integration adds the same `if (name in phaseOutputs && phasePassed(...)) continue` guard the resume loops already use, so seeded phases are elided.
- **Cheap gates always re-run.** `buildResumePlan` never lists `verify-scoped`, `lint-check`, or `typecheck-check` in its skip set — these re-execute on resume to re-confirm the working tree is still green. If a re-run gate fails, the seeded green agent work is stale; the plan is discarded and the story runs from its first non-green phase (existing short-circuit behavior).
- **Git-tree guard.** Each record carries the HEAD sha (`captureGitRef(workdir)`, `src/utils/git.ts:90`) and a working-tree digest (from `git status --porcelain`). `buildResumePlan` returns an empty skip set (full rerun for that story) when the current tree state does not match the checkpoint's — so resume never skips over a tree that moved between attempts.

**Scope** — In: `recordGreen` hook after each passing phase; seeding `phaseOutputs` from `buildResumePlan`; a canonical-loop skip guard; cheap gates always re-run; tree-state capture via `captureGitRef` + `git status --porcelain`; `resume-hydrate.ts` helper. Out: CLI command registration, replay-derived checkpointing, and mid-phase resume.

**Interface**
```typescript
runPhase(ctx, slot, phaseCosts, phaseOutputs, isThreeSession, opts?)
phasePassed(opName, output, storyId?): boolean
```

Before the main loop, seed `phaseOutputs[phase] = { success: true }` for each skip.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a story run with no prior checkpoint, when a canonical phase passes, then that phase is still dispatched through `runPhase` and triggers exactly one `recordGreen` call whose `phase` argument equals that phase's op name.
Given a phase whose output makes `phasePassed` return false, when the orchestrator handles that phase, then it does not call `recordGreen` for that phase.

Given a resume where `buildResumePlan` yields `skipPhases: ["test-writer", "implementer"]`, when the orchestrator runs, then `test-writer` and `implementer` are not dispatched through `runPhase` while a non-skipped agent phase still is.

Given a phase seeded from a resume plan, when `phasePassed(phase, phaseOutputs[phase], storyId)` and `extractPhaseFindings(phaseOutputs[phase])` are evaluated, then `phasePassed` returns true and `extractPhaseFindings` returns an empty array.

Given a resume plan, when the orchestrator resumes, then each cheap gate in `revalidateGates` (`verify-scoped`, `lint-check`, `typecheck-check`) is dispatched through `runPhase` even though the story is resuming.

Given a resume where a re-run cheap gate returns a failing output, when the orchestrator processes that gate, then it short-circuits the canonical loop at that gate and does not dispatch any later phase.
Given the resume path for a story, when the orchestrator starts that story, then it calls `buildResumePlan` once and seeds `phaseOutputs` from the returned `skipPhases`.

Given stubbed git helpers, when the tree-state capture helper runs, then it returns a `TreeState` whose `headSha` equals the value from `captureGitRef` and whose `dirtyDigest` is derived from the `git status --porcelain` output without using real git.
Given a checkpoint log emitted during orchestrator resume handling, when the log entry includes story metadata, then the data object lists `storyId` before any other checkpoint-specific fields.

routing.reasoning: This story changes a central orchestrator loop plus git-state capture and resume hydration, so it needs stronger isolation than simple TDD but does not rise to a repo-wide architectural rewrite.

userStories.title: Expose Resume Through CLI And Run Defaults
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the explicit `nax resume` command and wire auto-resume plus opt-out flags into `nax run`.

**Motivation** — crash recovery in nax is implicit, but nothing sub-story is persisted, so rerunning `nax run` restarts every incomplete story from the top of the 12-phase `CANONICAL_ORDER`.

**Approach** — `nax resume [-f <feature>]`:

- **stdout:** a one-line resume summary — the feature, the number of stories with a checkpoint, and the phases being skipped — then the normal run output.
- **stderr:** warnings and errors only (mirrors existing commands).
- **Exit codes:** `0` on a run that completes green; non-zero on run failure — the same code the underlying `nax run` returns. `nax resume` for a feature with **no** `checkpoint.jsonl` is not an error: it prints "No checkpoint found — running from scratch" and proceeds as a full `nax run` (exit `0`).
- **`nax run`** auto-resumes when a `checkpoint.jsonl` exists for the feature. `--fresh` / `--no-resume` truncates/ignores the checkpoint and runs every incomplete story from scratch.

**Scope** — In: `registerResumeCommand(program)` in `src/commands/resume.ts`, wiring it in `bin/nax.ts`, `nax run` auto-resume detection via `loadCheckpoints`, and `--fresh` / `--no-resume` that truncate or ignore `checkpoint.jsonl`. Out: persistent config fields, alternate replay-driven resume, or changes to run exit-code semantics.

**Interface**
```typescript
export function registerResumeCommand(program: Command): void
```

`nax resume` follows the same pattern via an exported `registerResumeCommand(program)`.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a fresh commander program, when `registerResumeCommand(program)` is called, then `program.commands` includes a command named `resume`.
Given a feature whose `checkpoint.jsonl` is absent, when `resume` runs for that feature, then it prints `No checkpoint found — running from scratch` to stdout and exits with code `0`.
Given a feature with a checkpoint, when `resume` runs, then it prints a resume summary line naming the feature and the count of stories with a checkpoint before the run output.
Given `nax run` for a feature with an existing `checkpoint.jsonl`, when the run starts, then it calls `loadCheckpoints` with that feature's `featureDir`.

Given `nax run` invoked with `--fresh` and an existing `checkpoint.jsonl`, when the run starts, then the checkpoint is truncated or ignored so `loadCheckpoints` or the seeding path yields no skip phases for any story.
Given `nax run` invoked with `--no-resume`, when the run starts, then it behaves identically to `--fresh` for producing an empty resume plan with no phases skipped.

routing.reasoning: This story follows existing commander registration and run-command wiring patterns across a small set of files, so medium complexity with standard TDD is the realistic fit.

analysis:
This feature is an enhancement to the existing run/orchestrator pipeline, not a greenfield slice. The main execution seam is `ExecutionPlan.run()` in `src/execution/story-orchestrator/execution-plan.ts:43`, which initializes `phaseOutputs` at `:45`, runs the canonical loop at `:63-89`, and already contains two later resume-style loops that skip phases when `name in phaseOutputs && phasePassed(...)` at `:121-125` and `:193-195`. That existing pattern materially lowers risk for the resume integration because the feature can seed the same in-memory skip state instead of inventing a second orchestration path. `runPhase()` in `src/execution/story-orchestrator/run-phase.ts:111-216` is the correct post-phase hook point because it writes `phaseOutputs[opName] = output` at `:156` and returns control to the main loop after the phase outcome is fully known. `phasePassed()` and `extractPhaseFindings()` in `src/execution/story-orchestrator/phase-eval.ts:19-97` are compatible with resume seeding today: a sentinel `{ success: true }` passes because `phasePassed()` accepts any object with `success !== false` at `:42-44`, and `extractPhaseFindings()` returns `[]` for a successful record at `:94-96`, which avoids phantom findings. The canonical phase list and cheap-gate set are grounded in `PhaseKind` and `CANONICAL_ORDER` in `src/execution/story-orchestrator/types.ts:65-77` and `:135-148`; the phases that must always re-run are the existing `verify-scoped`, `lint-check`, and `typecheck-check` entries at `:143-145`.

The new checkpoint data should live beside existing feature-scoped runtime artifacts. Feature directory plumbing already exists in `CrashRecoveryContext.featureDir` in `src/execution/crash-recovery.ts:35-58` and in `StatusWriter.writeFeatureStatus()` which writes `join(featureDir, "status.json")` in `src/execution/status-writer.ts:254-280`, especially `:262`. The current durable crash path uses synchronous append only inside crash handlers in `src/execution/crash-writer.ts:5-35` and `:55-88`; those comments explicitly justify `appendFileSync` only because the event loop may be inconsistent in a fatal signal path. That means the new normal-path checkpoint writer must not copy `node:fs` sync I/O into `src/` runtime code. The repo rule in `.claude/rules/forbidden-patterns.md` bans `fs.readFileSync` / `fs.writeFileSync` in source code in favor of Bun-native I/O, so the checkpoint writer needs its own injected async append dependency and Bun-native implementation rather than reusing the crash writer literally. This is the main architecture constraint in US-001 and US-003.

Git tree capture should reuse the existing Bun-native subprocess abstraction instead of adding direct `Bun.spawn` or Node child process calls. `src/utils/git.ts:14` exposes `_gitDeps = { spawn, getSafeLogger }`, `gitWithTimeout()` centralizes process handling at `:45-70`, and `captureGitRef()` already returns `HEAD` at `:90-98`. The spec’s dirty-tree digest can be built through the same `_gitDeps.spawn` path so unit tests can stub git output without real repos. That new helper is most naturally added either in `src/utils/git.ts` or a checkpoint-local helper that imports `_gitDeps`; whichever approach is chosen, it needs to preserve the repo’s dependency-injection pattern and avoid direct subprocess creation. Risk here is mostly around testability and keeping the helper pure enough for planner tests while still capturing actual working-tree state.

CLI impact is concentrated in `bin/nax.ts` and the existing replay command pattern. The main `run` command resolves `featureDir` and `prdPath` in `bin/nax.ts:523-524`, computes the output directory at `:618-624`, and calls the execution entrypoint at `:761-778`. That is the likely insertion point for auto-resume detection, `--fresh`, and `--no-resume` propagation. `registerReplayCommand()` in `src/commands/replay.ts:163-184` is the exact template for `registerResumeCommand()`, and replay’s orchestrator/deps split in `src/commands/replay.ts:30-158` is a useful model for a thin, hermetic CLI surface with explicit stdout/stderr handling. The replay tests already assert commander registration and option shape in `test/unit/commands/replay.test.ts:225-252`, so the resume command should mirror that style instead of inventing a different test harness. `bin/nax.ts:1486` wires replay into the root program; resume should be registered adjacent to that. One additional risk is that `bin/nax.ts` is already large and cross-cutting, so the PRD should keep the CLI story narrowly focused on flag parsing and delegating to existing helpers rather than broad run-command refactors.

Existing tests show both where to add coverage and what behavioral seams already exist. The graph trace shows `ExecutionPlan.run()` is already exercised by `test/unit/execution/story-orchestrator.test.ts`, several integration tests, and the E2E orchestrator harness. `test/helpers/e2e/orchestrator-harness.ts:1-220` records ordered phase execution by wrapping `_storyOrchestratorDeps.callOp`, which is useful for resume assertions because it can prove skipped phases were not dispatched. `test/e2e/resume.e2e.test.ts:25-84` already uses the term "resume," but it covers post-rectification resume inside a single process, not the new mid-session resume across reruns; that overlap is a naming and conceptual risk because implementers must avoid regressing current rectification-resume semantics while adding process-restart resume. The new feature should add unit/integration coverage close to the current command and orchestrator suites instead of a separate broad E2E path unless a specific full-run scenario is required by the ACs.

Likely files to modify: `src/execution/story-orchestrator/execution-plan.ts` for seeding and skip guards, `src/utils/git.ts` or a new checkpoint helper for dirty-tree capture, `bin/nax.ts` for flag parsing and auto-resume plumbing, and a new `src/commands/resume.ts` modeled on replay. Likely new files: `src/execution/checkpoint/types.ts`, `writer.ts`, `reader.ts`, `resume-plan.ts`, `resume-hydrate.ts`, and `index.ts`. Likely dependent/importing files: the execution barrel that re-exports orchestrator utilities if checkpoint APIs need public imports, `bin/nax.ts` for command registration, and tests under `test/unit/commands/` and `test/unit` or `test/integration/execution/` depending on seam. Backward compatibility risk is low because default behavior should remain a full rerun when no checkpoint exists, the checkpoint file is corrupt, or the tree guard fails. Migration path is also low risk: no schema migration is needed for existing features because a missing `checkpoint.jsonl` is treated as empty and `nax run` continues with today’s behavior. The main correctness risks are stale green phases being skipped after tree movement, writing checkpoints before a phase is actually green, and violating Bun-native source constraints by introducing Node sync file APIs on the normal execution path.
